raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On GLM-5.3-Flash MXFP4 (TP4, MI355X/gfx950) with the AITER FlashKDA prefill route from #63568 (`--kda-prefill-backend flashkda`), the 34 KDA layers of the most common prefill step, one 8192-token chunk with 8-15 decodes, take 44.0 ms of the 135.8 ms step. FlashKDA's kernels take 15.95 ms of that: FlashKDA counts each decode as a sequence when it plans its recurrence, so it stops segmenting, and its last pass walks the prefill's 256 chunks one after another (410 us per layer). Outside the input and output projections, most of the rest is the q|k|v conv (85 us per layer), copies that pack q, k, g and v for FlashKDA (52 us per layer), and `f_b` and `g_b` as two GEMMs.

This PR, with [ROCm/aiter#7084](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7084), takes those KDA layers from 44.00 to 32.20 ms per step (FlashKDA from 15.95 to 5.52 ms), and the step from 135.8 to 122.1 ms (-10.1%). Over nine serving points, output throughput is -0.2% to +9.4% (geomean +4.4%), median TPOT -0.2% to -7.7% (geomean -4.4%) and median TTFT -8.6% as a geomean. GPQA Diamond is 0.919 against the baseline's 0.909, GSM8K 0.915 against 0.918 over four runs each, and NIAH at 65536 is 1.0 in both.

## Modifications

- **A. Pass FlashKDA only the prefills:** FlashKDA 15.95 → 5.5 ms per common prefill step, and all 34 layers segment again.
- **B. Run `f_b` and `g_b` as one batched GEMM:** 310 → 176 us per decode step at batch 16.
- **C. Read strided q, k, g and v in place on gfx950** (AITER, [ROCm/aiter#7084](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7084)): copies 52.2 → 5.5 us per layer, 1.6 ms per common prefill step.
- **D. Use AITER's HIP prefill conv on gfx950:** conv 85.1 → 72.1 us per layer, 0.44 ms per common prefill step.

**A. Pass FlashKDA only the prefills** (`kda.py`). FlashKDA plans its recurrence from the block count over all sequences in the call: [`_choose_chunks_per_seg`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/1dd826c42b38aa71adf058053b9c512a9b47d20f/aiter/ops/triton/_triton_kernels/kimi_delta_attn/flash_kda.py#L1047-L1079) computes `blocks = n_seqs * H * max(1, V // 32)` and turns segmentation off when that exceeds the CU count. #63568 passes `non_spec_query_start_loc`, so each decode counts as a one-token sequence. At 16 KDA heads per rank each sequence is 64 blocks, so one prefill with four or more decodes passes 256 CUs, and with one to three decodes FlashKDA still segments but sizes the segments for the extra sequences. A mixed step now runs its leading decodes through the same `fused_recurrent_kda` call as a plain decode step, and passes FlashKDA only the prefills, with the metadata builder's prefill-only [`prefill_query_start_loc`, `prefill_state_indices` and `prefill_has_initial_state`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f5146b5b3a5b3c89ceee6f804e5e535a72ccbb/vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py#L122-L125). Both kernels update the paged recurrent state in place and write their slices straight into the layer output; [Kimi-K3's ROCm layer](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f5146b5b3a5b3c89ceee6f804e5e535a72ccbb/vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/kda.py#L651-L695) splits its decodes off the AITER prefill the same way. Steps with spec-decode tokens keep the Triton chunk path, as in #63568. The two kernels compute the same recurrence, so the outputs agree to bf16.

**B. Run `f_b` and `g_b` as one batched GEMM** (`kda.py`). `f_b` and `g_b` read adjacent column slices of the same projection, and launched one after the other: 4.5 and 4.6 us per layer at 16 decode tokens. When [`is_tgemm_enabled()`](https://github.com/waqahmed-amd-fi/vllm/blob/58caa1d025f04958507ce15fae125855f170c89f/vllm/_aiter_ops.py#L2641-L2644) is true (gfx950 with AITER linear) and both projections use `UnquantizedLinearMethod`, their weights are views of one `[2, N, K]` buffer, which loading fills in place, and forward runs one `torch.bmm` against it at every token count: one 5.2 us GEMM per layer at decode. At an 8192-token prefill the server's `bmm` takes 33.7 us per layer against 29.6 us for the two calls, about 0.14 ms per prefill step; a one-GPU run of the same call takes 28.3 us against 29.3 us. Quantized projections, and builds where AITER's tuned GEMM is off, keep the two linear calls.

**C. Read strided q, k, g and v in place on gfx950** (AITER only: [ROCm/aiter#7084](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7084), commit [d24a8a87](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/d24a8a8743e68ccccac7c893197a5a2c1934549d)). vLLM passes q, k and v as column slices of the merged conv output, at a token stride of 3 × H × D. On gfx950 FlashKDA packed them, and g, before K1 and passes A and C, about 52 us per layer at 8192 tokens; the gfx1250 kernels already read them in place. The gfx950 K1 now takes `stride_q`, `stride_k` and `stride_g`, and passes A and C take `stride_v`. `flash_kda_fwd` decides each operand after the kernel routes are known, and still packs an operand that a Triton kernel reads, whose rows are not 16-byte aligned, or whose span needs more than 32-bit offsets. Strided inputs give the packed result bit for bit.

**D. Use AITER's HIP prefill conv on gfx950** (`kda.py`, `_aiter_ops.py`). vLLM's [`_causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f5146b5b3a5b3c89ceee6f804e5e535a72ccbb/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/causal_conv1d.py#L593-L633) runs the 6144-channel q|k|v conv in programs of 8 tokens by 256 channels, one bf16 per thread per token: 85 us per layer in the common prefill step, about 2.4 TB/s. A prefill step of 4096 tokens or more now calls AITER's HIP [`causal_conv1d_split_qkv_hip_fn`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/1dd826c42b38aa71adf058053b9c512a9b47d20f/aiter/ops/causal_conv1d_fwd_split_qkv.py#L90-L112) through the new `rocm_aiter_ops.causal_conv1d_prefill_split_qkv()`. It takes `causal_conv1d_fn`'s inputs, updates the conv state the same way, and returns q, k and v as contiguous tensors. The HIP kernel reads bf16 weights, while the layer's conv parameters are fp32 holding the checkpoint's bf16 values, so the first forward makes a bf16 copy of the merged weight and keeps it only if it equals the fp32 weight (one `torch.equal` per layer, under `gpu_sync_allowed()`); weights with true fp32 values keep vLLM's kernel. The wrapper runs 32-token tiles and builds their (sequence, chunk) schedule on the host from the metadata's 8-token one, as ceil(ceil(n / 8) / 4) = ceil(n / 32), once per step and without a device-to-host read. It passes `has_initial_state` as a uint8 view, which saves [AITER's cast](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/1dd826c42b38aa71adf058053b9c512a9b47d20f/aiter/ops/causal_conv1d_fwd_split_qkv.py#L140), a 4.3 us kernel per layer. Steps under 4096 tokens keep vLLM's kernel, which is as fast there: 27.5 against 27.3 us at 2716 tokens and 10.7 against 10.8 us at 576, on one GPU. q, k and v match `causal_conv1d_fn` to one bf16 rounding, and the conv state exactly. [Kimi-K3's ROCm layer](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f5146b5b3a5b3c89ceee6f804e5e535a72ccbb/vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/kda.py#L601-L617) calls AITER's Triton tile kernel for the same op, which takes 108-200 us for GLM's 6144 channels on one GPU.

### Impact on CUDA and on Other AMD Architectures

No change reaches CUDA. On ROCm:

| change | runs when |
| --- | --- |
| A | the AITER FlashKDA prefill route runs (gfx950, `--kda-prefill-backend flashkda`) and the step has no spec-decode tokens |
| B | `is_tgemm_enabled()` (gfx950 with AITER linear) and both projections are unquantized |
| C | AITER's gfx950 FlashKDA Gluon kernels get strided q, k, g or v that they can read |
| D | gfx950 with AITER on and its HIP conv importable, a width-4 conv without bias, a bf16 conv state, conv weights that hold bf16 values, and a prefill step of 4096 tokens or more |

Everything else keeps today's path: the Triton chunk path, the CUDA FlashKDA backend, spec-decode steps, quantized `f_b` and `g_b`, packed FlashKDA inputs, gfx1250 and AITER's Triton FlashKDA kernels, and `causal_conv1d_fn`. C changes no vLLM code; its strided inputs give the packed result bit for bit.

## Accuracy Tests

GPQA Diamond with sglang `run_eval` (thinking on, 100000 max tokens, temperature 1, top-p 0.95), and RULER NIAH (`niah_single_2` at 65536) and GSM8K (5-shot, all 1319 questions, through the completions endpoint) with `lm_eval`, on the server of the serving sweep below. One run per arm for GPQA and NIAH, and four for GSM8K:

| | baseline | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GPQA Diamond | 0.909 | 0.919 |
| NIAH (`niah_single_2`, 65536) | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| GSM8K strict-match, mean of 4 runs (range) | 0.918 (0.904-0.926) | 0.915 (0.911-0.917) |
| GSM8K flexible-extract, mean of 4 runs (range) | 0.918 (0.904-0.926) | 0.915 (0.911-0.920) |

Over the three GSM8K runs per arm that logged every answer, 149 questions were right only with the baseline and 143 only with this PR (strict-match, sign test p = 0.77). Each arm's own reruns disagree on 80 to 92 questions, as many as the two arms do. One GPQA run's standard error is about 0.02.

### Unit Tests

```bash
# On gfx950 with VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
python -m pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py

# C, from the AITER checkout
python -m pytest op_tests/triton_tests/kimi_delta_attn -q
```

`test_aiter_flashkda_prefill_matches_triton` runs with 0 and with 3 decodes ahead of two prefills, checks that FlashKDA receives only the prefill rows, and matches the Triton chunk path to bf16 (A). It runs with vLLM's conv, with AITER's, and with AITER's asked for on conv weights with true fp32 values, which must keep vLLM's kernel (D). `test_aiter_conv1d_prefill_matches_vllm` runs AITER's conv as the layer calls it, on a strided q|k|v block with both conv-state layouts, at 740 and 5040 tokens; it matches `causal_conv1d_fn` to bf16 and the conv state exactly, and checks the 32-token schedule built from vLLM's 8-token one (D). `test_aiter_decode_route_follows_replayed_step` checks that the AITER layer's `f_b` and `g_b` weights are views of one `[2, N, K]` buffer, and that a mixed step matches the two-GEMM layer bit for bit (B). On MI355X the file gives 17 passed and 14 skipped, the skips being NVIDIA-only tests. AITER's `op_tests/triton_tests/kimi_delta_attn` gives 157 passed and 1 skipped on gfx950; its `test_strided_operands_match_packed` checks that the gfx950 Gluon kernels read the projection bands in place and match packed inputs bit for bit (C). The tests for A and D need gfx950 and AITER and skip elsewhere, and the serving and accuracy runs below were done outside CI.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Environment

The baseline is vLLM [c50aca14](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c50aca14416ef29f6ed0ed256302f30646726dcd) with [#59478](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59478), [#63555](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63555), [#54061](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54061), [#63213](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63213), [#63214](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63214), [#63568](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63568), [#63612](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63612), [#63603](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63603) and [#63910](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63910), and AITER [1dd826c4](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/1dd826c42b38aa71adf058053b9c512a9b47d20f) with [ROCm/aiter#6912](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6912) and [ROCm/aiter#7049](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7049). This PR is the baseline with this PR's commits and AITER [d24a8a87](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/d24a8a8743e68ccccac7c893197a5a2c1934549d) ([ROCm/aiter#7084](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7084)). Both use the same image and server command.

```console
GPU:    4x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950, 256 CUs), TP4
Image:  vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-c50aca14416ef29f6ed0ed256302f30646726dcd (torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, Triton 3.8)
Model:  amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 (MXFP4 MoE, fp8_e4m3 KV cache)
```

```bash
# Server, both arms (AITER is the AITER checkout)
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=1 \
  VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8=1 \
  SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0 VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=10800 \
  AITER_CONFIG_FMOE=$AITER/aiter/configs/model_configs/glm5_fp4_tuned_fmoe.csv:$AITER/aiter/configs/model_configs/glm53flash_fp4_tuned_fmoe.csv
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 --port 8364 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len 258048 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 128}' \
  --no-enable-log-requests --compilation-config '{"custom_ops": ["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \
  --monokernel --kda-prefill-backend flashkda

# One sweep point (60000/600, conc 16). The table below gives the others' lengths, concurrency and
# prompts; each point uses its own seed and warms up with as many requests as its concurrency.
python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --dataset-name random --port 8364 \
  --model amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 --tokenizer zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --random-range-ratio 0.8 \
  --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 16 --num-prompts 96 --random-input-len 60000 \
  --random-output-len 600 --seed 17 --warmup-requests 16

# Accuracy
python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gpqa --port 8364 --model amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --max-tokens 100000 --num-threads 64 --temperature 1 --top-p 0.95 \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": true, "think_end_token": "</think>"}'
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks niah_single_2 --metadata '{"max_seq_lengths":[65536]}' \
  --batch_size auto --seed 1234 \
  --model_args '{"model":"amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4","tokenizer":"zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash","base_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8364/v1/completions","num_concurrent":32,"tokenized_requests":false,"timeout":3600,"max_retries":1}'
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto --seed 1234 \
  --model_args '{"model":"amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4","tokenizer":"zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash","base_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8364/v1/completions","num_concurrent":64,"tokenized_requests":false,"timeout":3600,"max_retries":1}'
```

### Profile

Rank 0, torch profiler over the 60000/600 conc 16 benchmark, the 34 KDA layers of each full 8192-token prefill step, grouped by the decodes that ride along. Most such steps are one prefill with 8-15 decodes (194 of 260 in the baseline, 193 of 260 with this PR).

| | baseline | this PR | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| common prefill step | 135.8 ms | **122.1 ms** | **-10.1%** |
| its 34 KDA layers | 44.00 ms | **32.20 ms** | **-26.8%** |
| its FlashKDA kernels | 15.95 ms | **5.52 ms** | **-65.4%** |
| its layers segmented | 0 of 34 | **34 of 34** | |
| `f_b` and `g_b` GEMMs per decode step, batch 16 | 310 us | **176 us** | **-43.2%** |

Per KDA layer in the common prefill step, us:

| Kernel | baseline | this PR | From |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| FlashKDA pass C | 410.0 | 40.9 | A |
| FlashKDA pass A | — | 42.0 | A |
| FlashKDA segment scan | — | 23.3 | A |
| decodes' `fused_recurrent_kda` | — | 10.6 | A |
| `f_b` and `g_b` GEMMs | 29.6 (two calls) | 33.7 (one `bmm`) | B |
| copies | 52.2 | 5.5 | C |
| q\|k\|v conv | 85.1 (`_causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel`) | 72.1 (`conv1d_split_qkv_channel_last_t<32>`) | D |
| FlashKDA K1 | 59.0 | 56.1 | untouched |
| gated norm | 27.9 | 27.0 | untouched |
| in_proj GEMM | 311.4 | 309.9 | untouched |
| o_proj GEMM | 102.9 | 101.9 | untouched |
| all-reduce | 216.0 | 224.0 | untouched |
| **34 layers, ms per step** | **44.00** | **32.20 (-26.8%)** | |

The copies left include the `beta` pack in AITER's FlashKDA wrapper. Every batch mix segments all 34 layers with this PR:

| Batch mix | steps, baseline / this PR | layers segmented | FlashKDA ms | 34 KDA layers ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 prefill + 1-3 decodes | 20 / 21 | 34 → 34 | 9.90 → 5.50 | 38.17 → 31.81 |
| 1 prefill + 4-7 decodes | 27 / 27 | 0 → 34 | 15.63 → 5.50 | 43.74 → 31.87 |
| 1 prefill + 8-15 decodes | 194 / 193 | 0 → 34 | 15.95 → 5.52 | 44.00 → 32.20 |
| 2 prefills + 1-3 decodes | 3 / 3 | 22.7 → 34 | 8.91 → 6.97 | 37.09 → 33.29 |
| 2 prefills + 4-7 decodes | 4 / 4 | 0 → 34 | 13.63 → 6.97 | 41.77 → 33.34 |
| 2 prefills + 8-15 decodes | 12 / 12 | 0 → 34 | 13.07 → 6.93 | 41.06 → 33.34 |

Decode-only steps do not take the FlashKDA path; on them, B is the `f_b` and `g_b` row of the first table.

### Serving Sweep

sglang 0.5.18 `bench_serving`, random dataset, range ratio 0.8, nine points. The two arms ran interleaved, two rounds each; the numbers are means of the rounds.

| ISL / OSL | conc | prompts | output tok/s | median TPOT ms | median TTFT ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8192 / 1024 | 1 | 8 | 217 → 217 (+0.2%) | 4.48 → 4.47 (-0.2%) | 122 → 121 (-0.3%) |
| 8192 / 1024 | 4 | 32 | 738 → 745 (+1.0%) | 5.19 → 5.13 (-1.0%) | 129 → 123 (-4.1%) |
| 8192 / 1024 | 16 | 96 | 1678 → 1675 (-0.2%) | 9.12 → 9.01 (-1.1%) | 144 → 135 (-6.3%) |
| 8192 / 1024 | 64 | 256 | 3376 → 3565 (+5.6%) | 17.90 → 16.87 (-5.8%) | 260 → 234 (-9.9%) |
| 60000 / 600 | 4 | 32 | 351 → 362 (+3.1%) | 9.40 → 9.13 (-2.8%) | 922 → 885 (-4.1%) |
| 60000 / 600 | 8 | 64 | 418 → 443 (+5.9%) | 16.73 → 15.80 (-5.6%) | 984 → 908 (-7.7%) |
| 60000 / 600 | 16 | 96 | 503 → 540 (+7.4%) | 27.89 → 25.92 (-7.1%) | 1586 → 1403 (-11.5%) |
| 60000 / 600 | 32 | 128 | 557 → 610 (+9.4%) | 51.59 → 47.63 (-7.7%) | 2502 → 1951 (-22.0%) |
| 128000 / 1024 | 16 | 96 | 397 → 427 (+7.6%) | 36.09 → 33.30 (-7.7%) | 3289 → 2985 (-9.2%) |
| **geomean** | | | **+4.4%** | **-4.4%** | **-8.6%** |

The gains are largest at the long-context points and at 8192/1024 conc 64, where full prefill steps take more of the run; at 8192/1024 conc 1-16 throughput and TPOT move by about 1% or less. Rounds agree within 0.4% on throughput at every point except this PR's 8192/1024 conc 16 (3.2%), and within 1.7% on TPOT. Median TTFT varies by up to 26% between the baseline's rounds at 60000/600 conc 16 and 128000/1024 conc 16.

## Related Work

- Follow-up to #63568, which adds the ROCm AITER FlashKDA prefill route; this PR is stacked on it, and A applies to #63568's head [48af33a](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63568/commits/48af33a4d1fff8729297c44c99148d091c97582d) as is.
- Needs [ROCm/aiter#7084](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7084) for C. A, B and D work without it.
- Not a duplicate: #63568's head still passes the decodes to FlashKDA, open-PR searches for "FlashKDA decode", `kda_flashkda_prefill` and `causal_conv1d_split_qkv` find only #63568, and [#50226](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50226) speeds up the GDN causal-conv prefill on NVIDIA SM103, not this path.

## Future Work

- AITER: plan segments from the sequences long enough to segment, so callers that keep decodes in the FlashKDA call do not lose segmentation.
- Pass the prefill-only host bounds to FlashKDA as `cu_seqlens_cpu` once [ROCm/aiter#6912](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6912) lands, so AITER no longer reads `cu_seqlens` from the GPU in every KDA layer.
- Select AITER FlashKDA for `--kda-prefill-backend auto` on gfx950 when its checks pass.
- At prefill sizes, keep the two `f_b` and `g_b` calls, which are about 0.14 ms per prefill step faster there. A size check has to live in a custom op, because `torch.compile` freezes a Python branch.

detail.body:
## Motivation

On GLM-5.3-Flash MXFP4 (TP4, MI355X/gfx950) with the AITER FlashKDA prefill route from #63568 (`--kda-prefill-backend flashkda`), the 34 KDA layers of the most common prefill step, one 8192-token chunk with 8-15 decodes, take 44.0 ms of the 135.8 ms step. FlashKDA's kernels take 15.95 ms of that: FlashKDA counts each decode as a sequence when it plans its recurrence, so it stops segmenting, and its last pass walks the prefill's 256 chunks one after another (410 us per layer). Outside the input and output projections, most of the rest is the q|k|v conv (85 us per layer), copies that pack q, k, g and v for FlashKDA (52 us per layer), and `f_b` and `g_b` as two GEMMs.

This PR, with [ROCm/aiter#7084](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7084), takes those KDA layers from 44.00 to 32.20 ms per step (FlashKDA from 15.95 to 5.52 ms), and the step from 135.8 to 122.1 ms (-10.1%). Over nine serving points, output throughput is -0.2% to +9.4% (geomean +4.4%), median TPOT -0.2% to -7.7% (geomean -4.4%) and median TTFT -8.6% as a geomean. GPQA Diamond is 0.919 against the baseline's 0.909, GSM8K 0.915 against 0.918 over four runs each, and NIAH at 65536 is 1.0 in both.

## Modifications

- **A. Pass FlashKDA only the prefills:** FlashKDA 15.95 → 5.5 ms per common prefill step, and all 34 layers segment again.
- **B. Run `f_b` and `g_b` as one batched GEMM:** 310 → 176 us per decode step at batch 16.
- **C. Read strided q, k, g and v in place on gfx950** (AITER, [ROCm/aiter#7084](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7084)): copies 52.2 → 5.5 us per layer, 1.6 ms per common prefill step.
- **D. Use AITER's HIP prefill conv on gfx950:** conv 85.1 → 72.1 us per layer, 0.44 ms per common prefill step.

**A. Pass FlashKDA only the prefills** (`kda.py`). FlashKDA plans its recurrence from the block count over all sequences in the call: [`_choose_chunks_per_seg`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/1dd826c42b38aa71adf058053b9c512a9b47d20f/aiter/ops/triton/_triton_kernels/kimi_delta_attn/flash_kda.py#L1047-L1079) computes `blocks = n_seqs * H * max(1, V // 32)` and turns segmentation off when that exceeds the CU count. #63568 passes `non_spec_query_start_loc`, so each decode counts as a one-token sequence. At 16 KDA heads per rank each sequence is 64 blocks, so one prefill with four or more decodes passes 256 CUs, and with one to three decodes FlashKDA still segments but sizes the segments for the extra sequences. A mixed step now runs its leading decodes through the same `fused_recurrent_kda` call as a plain decode step, and passes FlashKDA only the prefills, with the metadata builder's prefill-only [`prefill_query_start_loc`, `prefill_state_indices` and `prefill_has_initial_state`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f5146b5b3a5b3c89ceee6f804e5e535a72ccbb/vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py#L122-L125). Both kernels update the paged recurrent state in place and write their slices straight into the layer output; [Kimi-K3's ROCm layer](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f5146b5b3a5b3c89ceee6f804e5e535a72ccbb/vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/kda.py#L651-L695) splits its decodes off the AITER prefill the same way. Steps with spec-decode tokens keep the Triton chunk path, as in #63568. The two kernels compute the same recurrence, so the outputs agree to bf16.

**B. Run `f_b` and `g_b` as one batched GEMM** (`kda.py`). `f_b` and `g_b` read adjacent column slices of the same projection, and launched one after the other: 4.5 and 4.6 us per layer at 16 decode tokens. When [`is_tgemm_enabled()`](https://github.com/waqahmed-amd-fi/vllm/blob/58caa1d025f04958507ce15fae125855f170c89f/vllm/_aiter_ops.py#L2641-L2644) is true (gfx950 with AITER linear) and both projections use `UnquantizedLinearMethod`, their weights are views of one `[2, N, K]` buffer, which loading fills in place, and forward runs one `torch.bmm` against it at every token count: one 5.2 us GEMM per layer at decode. At an 8192-token prefill the server's `bmm` takes 33.7 us per layer against 29.6 us for the two calls, about 0.14 ms per prefill step; a one-GPU run of the same call takes 28.3 us against 29.3 us. Quantized projections, and builds where AITER's tuned GEMM is off, keep the two linear calls.

**C. Read strided q, k, g and v in place on gfx950** (AITER only: [ROCm/aiter#7084](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7084), commit [d24a8a87](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/d24a8a8743e68ccccac7c893197a5a2c1934549d)). vLLM passes q, k and v as column slices of the merged conv output, at a token stride of 3 × H × D. On gfx950 FlashKDA packed them, and g, before K1 and passes A and C, about 52 us per layer at 8192 tokens; the gfx1250 kernels already read them in place. The gfx950 K1 now takes `stride_q`, `stride_k` and `stride_g`, and passes A and C take `stride_v`. `flash_kda_fwd` decides each operand after the kernel routes are known, and still packs an operand that a Triton kernel reads, whose rows are not 16-byte aligned, or whose span needs more than 32-bit offsets. Strided inputs give the packed result bit for bit.

**D. Use AITER's HIP prefill conv on gfx950** (`kda.py`, `_aiter_ops.py`). vLLM's [`_causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f5146b5b3a5b3c89ceee6f804e5e535a72ccbb/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/causal_conv1d.py#L593-L633) runs the 6144-channel q|k|v conv in programs of 8 tokens by 256 channels, one bf16 per thread per token: 85 us per layer in the common prefill step, about 2.4 TB/s. A prefill step of 4096 tokens or more now calls AITER's HIP [`causal_conv1d_split_qkv_hip_fn`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/1dd826c42b38aa71adf058053b9c512a9b47d20f/aiter/ops/causal_conv1d_fwd_split_qkv.py#L90-L112) through the new `rocm_aiter_ops.causal_conv1d_prefill_split_qkv()`. It takes `causal_conv1d_fn`'s inputs, updates the conv state the same way, and returns q, k and v as contiguous tensors. The HIP kernel reads bf16 weights, while the layer's conv parameters are fp32 holding the checkpoint's bf16 values, so the first forward makes a bf16 copy of the merged weight and keeps it only if it equals the fp32 weight (one `torch.equal` per layer, under `gpu_sync_allowed()`); weights with true fp32 values keep vLLM's kernel. The wrapper runs 32-token tiles and builds their (sequence, chunk) schedule on the host from the metadata's 8-token one, as ceil(ceil(n / 8) / 4) = ceil(n / 32), once per step and without a device-to-host read. It passes `has_initial_state` as a uint8 view, which saves [AITER's cast](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/1dd826c42b38aa71adf058053b9c512a9b47d20f/aiter/ops/causal_conv1d_fwd_split_qkv.py#L140), a 4.3 us kernel per layer. Steps under 4096 tokens keep vLLM's kernel, which is as fast there: 27.5 against 27.3 us at 2716 tokens and 10.7 against 10.8 us at 576, on one GPU. q, k and v match `causal_conv1d_fn` to one bf16 rounding, and the conv state exactly. [Kimi-K3's ROCm layer](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f5146b5b3a5b3c89ceee6f804e5e535a72ccbb/vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/kda.py#L601-L617) calls AITER's Triton tile kernel for the same op, which takes 108-200 us for GLM's 6144 channels on one GPU.

### Impact on CUDA and on Other AMD Architectures

No change reaches CUDA. On ROCm:

| change | runs when |
| --- | --- |
| A | the AITER FlashKDA prefill route runs (gfx950, `--kda-prefill-backend flashkda`) and the step has no spec-decode tokens |
| B | `is_tgemm_enabled()` (gfx950 with AITER linear) and both projections are unquantized |
| C | AITER's gfx950 FlashKDA Gluon kernels get strided q, k, g or v that they can read |
| D | gfx950 with AITER on and its HIP conv importable, a width-4 conv without bias, a bf16 conv state, conv weights that hold bf16 values, and a prefill step of 4096 tokens or more |

Everything else keeps today's path: the Triton chunk path, the CUDA FlashKDA backend, spec-decode steps, quantized `f_b` and `g_b`, packed FlashKDA inputs, gfx1250 and AITER's Triton FlashKDA kernels, and `causal_conv1d_fn`. C changes no vLLM code; its strided inputs give the packed result bit for bit.

## Accuracy Tests

GPQA Diamond with sglang `run_eval` (thinking on, 100000 max tokens, temperature 1, top-p 0.95), and RULER NIAH (`niah_single_2` at 65536) and GSM8K (5-shot, all 1319 questions, through the completions endpoint) with `lm_eval`, on the server of the serving sweep below. One run per arm for GPQA and NIAH, and four for GSM8K:

| | baseline | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GPQA Diamond | 0.909 | 0.919 |
| NIAH (`niah_single_2`, 65536) | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| GSM8K strict-match, mean of 4 runs (range) | 0.918 (0.904-0.926) | 0.915 (0.911-0.917) |
| GSM8K flexible-extract, mean of 4 runs (range) | 0.918 (0.904-0.926) | 0.915 (0.911-0.920) |

Over the three GSM8K runs per arm that logged every answer, 149 questions were right only with the baseline and 143 only with this PR (strict-match, sign test p = 0.77). Each arm's own reruns disagree on 80 to 92 questions, as many as the two arms do. One GPQA run's standard error is about 0.02.

### Unit Tests

```bash
# On gfx950 with VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
python -m pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py

# C, from the AITER checkout
python -m pytest op_tests/triton_tests/kimi_delta_attn -q
```

`test_aiter_flashkda_prefill_matches_triton` runs with 0 and with 3 decodes ahead of two prefills, checks that FlashKDA receives only the prefill rows, and matches the Triton chunk path to bf16 (A). It runs with vLLM's conv, with AITER's, and with AITER's asked for on conv weights with true fp32 values, which must keep vLLM's kernel (D). `test_aiter_conv1d_prefill_matches_vllm` runs AITER's conv as the layer calls it, on a strided q|k|v block with both conv-state layouts, at 740 and 5040 tokens; it matches `causal_conv1d_fn` to bf16 and the conv state exactly, and checks the 32-token schedule built from vLLM's 8-token one (D). `test_aiter_decode_route_follows_replayed_step` checks that the AITER layer's `f_b` and `g_b` weights are views of one `[2, N, K]` buffer, and that a mixed step matches the two-GEMM layer bit for bit (B). On MI355X the file gives 17 passed and 14 skipped, the skips being NVIDIA-only tests. AITER's `op_tests/triton_tests/kimi_delta_attn` gives 157 passed and 1 skipped on gfx950; its `test_strided_operands_match_packed` checks that the gfx950 Gluon kernels read the projection bands in place and match packed inputs bit for bit (C). The tests for A and D need gfx950 and AITER and skip elsewhere, and the serving and accuracy runs below were done outside CI.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Environment

The baseline is vLLM [c50aca14](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c50aca14416ef29f6ed0ed256302f30646726dcd) with [#59478](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59478), [#63555](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63555), [#54061](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54061), [#63213](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63213), [#63214](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63214), [#63568](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63568), [#63612](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63612), [#63603](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63603) and [#63910](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63910), and AITER [1dd826c4](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/1dd826c42b38aa71adf058053b9c512a9b47d20f) with [ROCm/aiter#6912](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6912) and [ROCm/aiter#7049](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7049). This PR is the baseline with this PR's commits and AITER [d24a8a87](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/d24a8a8743e68ccccac7c893197a5a2c1934549d) ([ROCm/aiter#7084](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7084)). Both use the same image and server command.

```console
GPU:    4x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950, 256 CUs), TP4
Image:  vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-c50aca14416ef29f6ed0ed256302f30646726dcd (torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, Triton 3.8)
Model:  amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 (MXFP4 MoE, fp8_e4m3 KV cache)
```

```bash
# Server, both arms (AITER is the AITER checkout)
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=1 \
  VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8=1 \
  SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0 VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=10800 \
  AITER_CONFIG_FMOE=$AITER/aiter/configs/model_configs/glm5_fp4_tuned_fmoe.csv:$AITER/aiter/configs/model_configs/glm53flash_fp4_tuned_fmoe.csv
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 --port 8364 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len 258048 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 128}' \
  --no-enable-log-requests --compilation-config '{"custom_ops": ["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \
  --monokernel --kda-prefill-backend flashkda

# One sweep point (60000/600, conc 16). The table below gives the others' lengths, concurrency and
# prompts; each point uses its own seed and warms up with as many requests as its concurrency.
python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --dataset-name random --port 8364 \
  --model amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 --tokenizer zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --random-range-ratio 0.8 \
  --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 16 --num-prompts 96 --random-input-len 60000 \
  --random-output-len 600 --seed 17 --warmup-requests 16

# Accuracy
python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gpqa --port 8364 --model amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --max-tokens 100000 --num-threads 64 --temperature 1 --top-p 0.95 \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": true, "think_end_token": "</think>"}'
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks niah_single_2 --metadata '{"max_seq_lengths":[65536]}' \
  --batch_size auto --seed 1234 \
  --model_args '{"model":"amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4","tokenizer":"zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash","base_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8364/v1/completions","num_concurrent":32,"tokenized_requests":false,"timeout":3600,"max_retries":1}'
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto --seed 1234 \
  --model_args '{"model":"amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4","tokenizer":"zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash","base_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8364/v1/completions","num_concurrent":64,"tokenized_requests":false,"timeout":3600,"max_retries":1}'
```

### Profile

Rank 0, torch profiler over the 60000/600 conc 16 benchmark, the 34 KDA layers of each full 8192-token prefill step, grouped by the decodes that ride along. Most such steps are one prefill with 8-15 decodes (194 of 260 in the baseline, 193 of 260 with this PR).

| | baseline | this PR | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| common prefill step | 135.8 ms | **122.1 ms** | **-10.1%** |
| its 34 KDA layers | 44.00 ms | **32.20 ms** | **-26.8%** |
| its FlashKDA kernels | 15.95 ms | **5.52 ms** | **-65.4%** |
| its layers segmented | 0 of 34 | **34 of 34** | |
| `f_b` and `g_b` GEMMs per decode step, batch 16 | 310 us | **176 us** | **-43.2%** |

Per KDA layer in the common prefill step, us:

| Kernel | baseline | this PR | From |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| FlashKDA pass C | 410.0 | 40.9 | A |
| FlashKDA pass A | — | 42.0 | A |
| FlashKDA segment scan | — | 23.3 | A |
| decodes' `fused_recurrent_kda` | — | 10.6 | A |
| `f_b` and `g_b` GEMMs | 29.6 (two calls) | 33.7 (one `bmm`) | B |
| copies | 52.2 | 5.5 | C |
| q\|k\|v conv | 85.1 (`_causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel`) | 72.1 (`conv1d_split_qkv_channel_last_t<32>`) | D |
| FlashKDA K1 | 59.0 | 56.1 | untouched |
| gated norm | 27.9 | 27.0 | untouched |
| in_proj GEMM | 311.4 | 309.9 | untouched |
| o_proj GEMM | 102.9 | 101.9 | untouched |
| all-reduce | 216.0 | 224.0 | untouched |
| **34 layers, ms per step** | **44.00** | **32.20 (-26.8%)** | |

The copies left include the `beta` pack in AITER's FlashKDA wrapper. Every batch mix segments all 34 layers with this PR:

| Batch mix | steps, baseline / this PR | layers segmented | FlashKDA ms | 34 KDA layers ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 prefill + 1-3 decodes | 20 / 21 | 34 → 34 | 9.90 → 5.50 | 38.17 → 31.81 |
| 1 prefill + 4-7 decodes | 27 / 27 | 0 → 34 | 15.63 → 5.50 | 43.74 → 31.87 |
| 1 prefill + 8-15 decodes | 194 / 193 | 0 → 34 | 15.95 → 5.52 | 44.00 → 32.20 |
| 2 prefills + 1-3 decodes | 3 / 3 | 22.7 → 34 | 8.91 → 6.97 | 37.09 → 33.29 |
| 2 prefills + 4-7 decodes | 4 / 4 | 0 → 34 | 13.63 → 6.97 | 41.77 → 33.34 |
| 2 prefills + 8-15 decodes | 12 / 12 | 0 → 34 | 13.07 → 6.93 | 41.06 → 33.34 |

Decode-only steps do not take the FlashKDA path; on them, B is the `f_b` and `g_b` row of the first table.

### Serving Sweep

sglang 0.5.18 `bench_serving`, random dataset, range ratio 0.8, nine points. The two arms ran interleaved, two rounds each; the numbers are means of the rounds.

| ISL / OSL | conc | prompts | output tok/s | median TPOT ms | median TTFT ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8192 / 1024 | 1 | 8 | 217 → 217 (+0.2%) | 4.48 → 4.47 (-0.2%) | 122 → 121 (-0.3%) |
| 8192 / 1024 | 4 | 32 | 738 → 745 (+1.0%) | 5.19 → 5.13 (-1.0%) | 129 → 123 (-4.1%) |
| 8192 / 1024 | 16 | 96 | 1678 → 1675 (-0.2%) | 9.12 → 9.01 (-1.1%) | 144 → 135 (-6.3%) |
| 8192 / 1024 | 64 | 256 | 3376 → 3565 (+5.6%) | 17.90 → 16.87 (-5.8%) | 260 → 234 (-9.9%) |
| 60000 / 600 | 4 | 32 | 351 → 362 (+3.1%) | 9.40 → 9.13 (-2.8%) | 922 → 885 (-4.1%) |
| 60000 / 600 | 8 | 64 | 418 → 443 (+5.9%) | 16.73 → 15.80 (-5.6%) | 984 → 908 (-7.7%) |
| 60000 / 600 | 16 | 96 | 503 → 540 (+7.4%) | 27.89 → 25.92 (-7.1%) | 1586 → 1403 (-11.5%) |
| 60000 / 600 | 32 | 128 | 557 → 610 (+9.4%) | 51.59 → 47.63 (-7.7%) | 2502 → 1951 (-22.0%) |
| 128000 / 1024 | 16 | 96 | 397 → 427 (+7.6%) | 36.09 → 33.30 (-7.7%) | 3289 → 2985 (-9.2%) |
| **geomean** | | | **+4.4%** | **-4.4%** | **-8.6%** |

The gains are largest at the long-context points and at 8192/1024 conc 64, where full prefill steps take more of the run; at 8192/1024 conc 1-16 throughput and TPOT move by about 1% or less. Rounds agree within 0.4% on throughput at every point except this PR's 8192/1024 conc 16 (3.2%), and within 1.7% on TPOT. Median TTFT varies by up to 26% between the baseline's rounds at 60000/600 conc 16 and 128000/1024 conc 16.

## Related Work

- Follow-up to #63568, which adds the ROCm AITER FlashKDA prefill route; this PR is stacked on it, and A applies to #63568's head [48af33a](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63568/commits/48af33a4d1fff8729297c44c99148d091c97582d) as is.
- Needs [ROCm/aiter#7084](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7084) for C. A, B and D work without it.
- Not a duplicate: #63568's head still passes the decodes to FlashKDA, open-PR searches for "FlashKDA decode", `kda_flashkda_prefill` and `causal_conv1d_split_qkv` find only #63568, and [#50226](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50226) speeds up the GDN causal-conv prefill on NVIDIA SM103, not this path.

## Future Work

- AITER: plan segments from the sequences long enough to segment, so callers that keep decodes in the FlashKDA call do not lose segmentation.
- Pass the prefill-only host bounds to FlashKDA as `cu_seqlens_cpu` once [ROCm/aiter#6912](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6912) lands, so AITER no longer reads `cu_seqlens` from the GPU in every KDA layer.
- Select AITER FlashKDA for `--kda-prefill-backend auto` on gfx950 when its checks pass.
- At prefill sizes, keep the two `f_b` and `g_b` calls, which are about 0.14 ms per prefill step faster there. A size check has to live in a custom op, because `torch.compile` freezes a Python branch.

@@ -0,0 +1,733 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""GLM-5.3-Flash whole-layer sparse-attention MonoKernel on CDNA4, a process a rank.
+
+Every stage is checked on the kernel's own inputs to it: the attention-side mHC,
+the q_a / kv_a / indexer projections, the norms and the MLA cache row, the kpool
+compression and tail ring (against vLLM's kpool kernel), q_b, the index query
+(against vLLM's FWHT FP8 quant), W_UK, the pool scores, the top-512 selection with
+its tail fit, the sparse attention and W_UV, then the FFN seam on the TP sum of the
+o_proj partials and the MoE. Rows mix short (every token), long (scored), pool
+completing and padding rows."""
+
+import torch
+
+from ._ffn import (
+    POLL_TIMEOUT_US,
+    REPLAYS,
+    _Layer,
+    _moe_reference,
+    _rel,
+    _vllm_seam,
+)
+
+ROWS = (2, 4, 8)
+BLOCK = 64  # MLA tokens a cache block: 16 kpool entries a block (preshuffled)
+MAX_LEN = 8192
+# tokens of each row including the new one (0: padding); 4100, 1500, 7000, 64 and
+# 6200 complete a pool, 2050 / 2049 / 3333 keep a 2 / 1 / 1-token tail
+LENS = (4100, 1500, 2050, 7000, 2049, 64, 3333)
+
+
+def _bf16(w):
+    wb = w.bfloat16().contiguous()
+    return wb, None, wb.float()
+
+
+def _fp8_block(w):
+    """FP8 E4M3 with f32 128 x 128 block scales: (q, scales, dequantized)."""
+    R, K = w.shape
+    wb = w.float().view(R // 128, 128, K // 128, 128)
+    s = wb.abs().amax((1, 3)) / 448.0 + 1e-12
+    q = (wb / s[:, None, :, None]).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    deq = (q.float() * s[:, None, :, None]).view(R, K)
+    return q.view(R, K), s.contiguous(), deq
+
+
+def _icache_perm(ipb: int, device) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Byte of (pool offset, dim) in an index-cache block (16 x 16-byte tiles)."""
+    off = torch.arange(ipb, device=device)[:, None]
+    d = torch.arange(128, device=device)[None, :]
+    if ipb == 1:
+        return (off * 128 + d).reshape(-1)
+    return ((off // 16) * 2048 + (d // 16) * 256 + (off % 16) * 16 + d % 16).reshape(-1)
+
+
+def _icache_read(cache):
+    """(values [NB, IPB, 128] f32, scales [NB, IPB]) of an index cache."""
+    nb, ipb = cache.shape[:2]
+    flat = cache.view(nb, -1)
+    vals = flat[:, _icache_perm(ipb, cache.device)].contiguous()
+    vals = vals.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float().view(nb, ipb, 128)
+    scales = flat[:, ipb * 128 :].contiguous().view(torch.float32)
+    return vals, scales
+
+
+class _Dsa:
+    """One sparse-attention layer's random weights (every rank builds the same) and
+    this rank's shard, in vLLM's post-load layouts."""
+
+    def __init__(self, rank: int, tp: int, device, fp8=(True, True, True)) -> None:
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.mono.config import (
+            HC_MULT,
+            HIDDEN,
+            INDEX_DIM,
+            INDEX_HEADS,
+            KV_LORA,
+            MLA_HEADS,
+            NOPE_DIM,
+            Q_LORA,
+            V_DIM,
+        )
+
+        g = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(2)
+        H = MLA_HEADS // tp
+        self.H, self.tp, self.rank = H, tp, rank
+
+        def rnd(*shape, scale=1.0):
+            return torch.randn(*shape, generator=g, device=device) * scale
+
+        nmix = HC_MULT * (2 + HC_MULT)
+        self.hc_fn = rnd(nmix, HC_MULT * HIDDEN, scale=0.01)
+        self.hc_scale = torch.rand(3, generator=g, device=device) + 0.5
+        self.hc_base = rnd(nmix, scale=0.1)
+        self.g_in = (1 + 0.1 * rnd(HIDDEN)).bfloat16()
+        quant = [_fp8_block if f else _bf16 for f in fp8]
+        self.w_qkv, self.s_qkv, self.d_qkv = quant[0](
+            rnd(Q_LORA + KV_LORA, HIDDEN, scale=HIDDEN**-0.5)
+        )
+        self.w_idx = rnd(INDEX_DIM + INDEX_HEADS, HIDDEN, scale=HIDDEN**-0.5).bfloat16()
+        self.w_gate = rnd(INDEX_DIM, HIDDEN, scale=HIDDEN**-0.5).bfloat16()
+        self.g_qa = (1 + 0.1 * rnd(Q_LORA)).bfloat16()
+        self.g_kv = (1 + 0.1 * rnd(KV_LORA)).bfloat16()
+        self.ln_w = 1 + 0.1 * rnd(INDEX_DIM)
+        self.ln_b = 0.1 * rnd(INDEX_DIM)
+        self.ape = 0.5 * rnd(4, INDEX_DIM)
+        q_b, s_qb, d_qb = quant[1](
+            rnd(MLA_HEADS * NOPE_DIM, Q_LORA, scale=Q_LORA**-0.5)
+        )
+        rows = slice(rank * H * NOPE_DIM, (rank + 1) * H * NOPE_DIM)
+        self.w_qb, self.d_qb = q_b[rows].contiguous(), d_qb[rows]
+        self.s_qb = (
+            None
+            if s_qb is None
+            else s_qb[rank * H * 2 : (rank + 1) * H * 2].contiguous()
+        )
+        self.w_iq = rnd(INDEX_HEADS * INDEX_DIM, Q_LORA, scale=Q_LORA**-0.5).bfloat16()
+        kv_b = rnd(MLA_HEADS * (NOPE_DIM + V_DIM), KV_LORA, scale=KV_LORA**-0.5)
+        per = NOPE_DIM + V_DIM
+        self.w_kvb = kv_b[rank * H * per : (rank + 1) * H * per].bfloat16().contiguous()
+        heads = self.w_kvb.view(H, per, KV_LORA)
+        self.w_uk = heads[:, :NOPE_DIM].transpose(1, 2).contiguous()  # [H, 512, 256]
+        self.w_uv = heads[:, NOPE_DIM:]  # [H, 256, 512]
+        w_o, s_o, d_o = quant[2](
+            rnd(HIDDEN, MLA_HEADS * V_DIM, scale=(MLA_HEADS * V_DIM) ** -0.5)
+        )
+        self.d_o_full = d_o
+        cols = slice(rank * H * V_DIM, (rank + 1) * H * V_DIM)
+        self.w_o = w_o[:, cols].contiguous()
+        self.s_o = (
+            None
+            if s_o is None
+            else s_o[:, rank * H * 2 : (rank + 1) * H * 2].contiguous()
+        )
+
+    def weights(self):
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.mono.ffn.op import (
+            FlashDsaWeights,
+        )
+
+        return FlashDsaWeights(
+            hc_fn=self.hc_fn,
+            hc_scale=self.hc_scale,
+            hc_base=self.hc_base,
+            g_norm=self.g_in,
+            w_qkv=self.w_qkv,
+            s_qkv=self.s_qkv,
+            w_idx=self.w_idx,
+            w_gate=self.w_gate,
+            g_qa=self.g_qa,
+            g_kv=self.g_kv,
+            ln_w=self.ln_w,
+            ln_b=self.ln_b,
+            ape=self.ape,
+            w_qb=self.w_qb,
+            s_qb=self.s_qb,
+            w_iq=self.w_iq,
+            w_uk=self.w_uk,
+            w_kvb=self.w_kvb,
+            w_o=self.w_o,
+            s_o=self.s_o,
+        )
+
+
+class _Caches:
+    """Random caches for S / tpr requests of up to MAX_LEN tokens, the block table,
+    and the step's row table: ``tpr`` rows a request (an MTP verify step: its
+    token and drafts at consecutive positions); the last request pads when there
+    is more than one."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        S: int,
+        device,
+        seed: int,
+        tpr: int = 1,
+        kv_fp8: bool = False,
+        max_len: int = MAX_LEN,
+        lens: tuple[int, ...] = LENS,
+    ) -> None:
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.mono.config import (
+            INDEX_DIM,
+            KV_LORA,
+        )
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.mono.ffn.layout import (
+            ROW_BT,
+            ROW_IBT,
+            ROW_WORDS,
+        )
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.runtime.spec import tail_ring
+
+        g = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(seed)
+        per = max_len // BLOCK
+        R = S // tpr
+        ring = tail_ring(tpr)
+        self.tpr, self.ring = tpr, ring
+        nb = 1 + R * per
+        ipb = BLOCK // 4
+        self.ipb = ipb
+        self.kv = torch.randn(nb, BLOCK, KV_LORA, generator=g, device=device).bfloat16()
+        # an e4m3 cache over a per-tensor scale (vLLM's _k_scale; not 1 here so
+        # the test sees it applied)
+        self.k_scale = None
+        if kv_fp8:
+            self.k_scale = torch.tensor([0.5], device=device)
+            self.kv = _e4m3(self.kv, self.k_scale)
+        vals = (torch.randn(nb, ipb, INDEX_DIM, generator=g, device=device) * 64).clamp(
+            -448, 448
+        )
+        scales = torch.exp2(
+            -torch.randint(6, 10, (nb, ipb), generator=g, device=device).float()
+        )
+        idx = torch.zeros(nb, ipb, INDEX_DIM + 4, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)
+        flat = idx.view(nb, -1)
+        flat[:, _icache_perm(ipb, device)] = (
+            vals.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).view(torch.uint8).view(nb, -1)
+        )
+        flat[:, ipb * INDEX_DIM :] = scales.view(torch.uint8).view(nb, -1)
+        self.idx = idx
+        self.tail = torch.randn(
+            R + 1, 2, ring, INDEX_DIM, generator=g, device=device
+        ).bfloat16()
+        perm = torch.randperm(nb - 1, generator=g, device=device) + 1
+        self.bt = perm[: R * per].view(R, per).int().contiguous()
+        lens = list(lens[: R - 1]) + [0] if R > 1 else [lens[0]]
+        self.lens = lens
+        rows = torch.full((S, ROW_WORDS), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+        for q, n in enumerate(lens):
+            for j in range(tpr):
+                r = q * tpr + j
+                rows[r, ROW_BT] = q
+                rows[r, ROW_IBT] = q
+                if n == 0:
+                    continue
+                pos = n - tpr + j
+                blk = int(self.bt[q, pos // BLOCK])
+                rows[r, 0] = pos
+                rows[r, 1] = blk * BLOCK + pos % BLOCK
+                rows[r, 2] = blk * ipb + (pos // 4) % ipb if pos % 4 == 3 else -1
+                rows[r, 3] = (q + 1) * ring + pos % ring
+        self.rows = rows
+
+    def caches(self):
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.mono.ffn.op import (
+            FlashDsaCaches,
+        )
+
+        return FlashDsaCaches(self.kv, self.idx, self.tail, self.k_scale)
+
+    def deq(self, rows: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Cache rows as fp32 values."""
+        if self.k_scale is None:
+            return rows.float()
+        return rows.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float() * self.k_scale
+
+    def clone(self):
+        c = object.__new__(_Caches)
+        c.__dict__.update(self.__dict__)
+        c.kv, c.idx, c.tail = self.kv.clone(), self.idx.clone(), self.tail.clone()
+        return c
+
+
+def _box(rt, name, n, packed=False):
+    """The first ``n`` values of a mailbox: f32 pairs, or packed bf16 pairs."""
+    words = rt.scratch[rt.sc[name] :].view(torch.int32)
+    if packed:
+        return words[:n:2].contiguous().view(torch.bfloat16)
+    return words[: 2 * n : 2].contiguous().view(torch.float32)
+
+
+def _rms(x, w, eps=1e-5):
+    x = x.float()
+    return (
+        x * torch.rsqrt(x.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True) + eps) * w.float()
+    ).bfloat16()
+
+
+def _e4m3(x: torch.Tensor, scale: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The fp8 MLA cache write of vLLM (``concat_and_cache_mla``): x / scale,
+    saturated to the e4m3 range, as raw bytes."""
+    e4m3 = (x.float() / scale).clamp(-448, 448).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    return e4m3.view(torch.uint8)
+
+
+def _check(rank: int, tp: int, device, fp8, tpr: int = 1, kv_fp8: bool = False) -> None:
+    import torch.distributed as dist
+    import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+    from vllm.distributed import get_tp_group
+    from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.ops.kpool_compress import (
+        kpool_decode_update_and_maybe_write_cache_batched,
+    )
+    from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.mono.config import (
+        HC_MULT,
+        HIDDEN,
+        INDEX_DIM,
+        INDEX_EPS,
+        INDEX_HEADS,
+        KV_LORA,
+        MLA_SCALE,
+        MOE_SLOTS,
+        NOPE_DIM,
+        Q_LORA,
+        TOPK_POOLS,
+        TOPK_TOKENS,
+        V_DIM,
+    )
+    from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.mono.ffn.op import (
+        FlashFfnOp,
+        FlashFfnRuntime,
+    )
+    from vllm.models.glm5next.nvidia.ops.kpool_compress import fwht128_quant_fp8
+
+    lay, dsa = _Layer(rank, tp, device), _Dsa(rank, tp, device, fp8)
+    H = dsa.H
+    group = get_tp_group().cpu_group
+    max_pools = MAX_LEN // 4
+    sizes = ROWS if tp > 2 else ROWS[:2]
+    if tpr > 1:
+        sizes = [r * tpr for r in (1, 2, 4) if r * tpr <= 8]
+    for S in sizes:
+        rt = FlashFfnRuntime(
+            S,
+            rank,
+            tp,

+    a, b = a.float().reshape(-1), b.float().reshape(-1)
+    return ((a - b).norm() / b.norm()).item()

+def _dequant(q, s):
+    fp4 = torch.tensor(_FP4, device=q.device)
+    v = torch.stack([fp4[(q & 15).long()], fp4[(q >> 4).long()]], -1).flatten(-2)
+    return v * torch.exp2(s.float() - 127).repeat_interleave(32, -1)

+def _mxfp8(a):
+    """The kernel's activation quant: per 32, e8m0 scale ceil(amax / 448), e4m3."""
+    shp, a = a.shape, a.float().reshape(-1, 32)
+    bits = (a.abs().amax(-1, keepdim=True) / 448.0).view(torch.int32)
+    e = (((bits >> 23) & 0xFF) + ((bits & 0x7FFFFF) != 0).int()).clamp(1, 254)
+    scale = torch.exp2(e.float() - 127)
+    q = (a / scale).clamp(-448, 448).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float()
+    return (q * scale).reshape(shp)
+

+def _moe_reference(x, w_r, bias, w13, w2, inter):
+    from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.mono.config import (
+        HIDDEN,
+        N_EXPERTS,
+        ROUTE_SCALE,
+        SWIGLU_LIMIT,
+        TOP_K,
+    )
+
+    scores = torch.sigmoid(x.float() @ w_r.float().T)
+    order = torch.argsort(-(scores + bias), dim=-1, stable=True)[:, :TOP_K]
+    picked = torch.gather(scores, 1, order)
+    weights = picked / picked.sum(-1, keepdim=True) * ROUTE_SCALE
+    out = torch.zeros(x.shape[0], HIDDEN, device=x.device)
+    xin = _mxfp8(x)
+    for s in range(x.shape[0]):
+        for e, wt in zip([N_EXPERTS] + order[s].tolist(), [1.0] + weights[s].tolist()):
+            gu = w13[e] @ xin[s]
+            gate = gu[:inter].clamp(max=SWIGLU_LIMIT)
+            up = gu[inter:].clamp(-SWIGLU_LIMIT, SWIGLU_LIMIT)
+            out[s] += wt * (w2[e] @ _mxfp8(torch.nn.functional.silu(gate) * up))
+    return out, order

+class _Layer:
+    """One layer's random weights (every rank builds the same) and this rank's shard."""
+
+    def __init__(self, rank: int, tp: int, device) -> None:
+        from aiter.ops.shuffle import shuffle_scale, shuffle_weight
+
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.mono.config import (
+            GLOBAL_INTER,
+            HC_MULT,
+            HIDDEN,
+            N_EXPERTS,
+        )
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.mono.packing import pack_bf16
+
+        g = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(0)
+        E, full, self.inter = N_EXPERTS + 1, GLOBAL_INTER, GLOBAL_INTER // tp
+
+        def mxfp4(rows, k):
+            q = torch.randint(0, 256, (E, rows, k // 2), generator=g, device=device)
+            s = torch.randint(119, 124, (E, rows, k // 32), generator=g, device=device)

+
+        def rows(t):
+            return torch.cat([t[:, lo:hi], t[:, full + lo : full + hi]], 1).contiguous()
+
+        self.k_w13 = shuffle_weight(rows(q13).view(fp4), layout=(16, 16))
+        self.k_s13 = shuffle_scale(rows(s13).view(E * 2 * n, -1)).view(E, 2 * n, -1)
+        self.k_w2 = shuffle_weight(
+            q2[:, :, lo // 2 : hi // 2].contiguous().view(fp4), layout=(16, 16)
+        )
+        self.k_s2 = shuffle_scale(
+            s2[:, :, lo // 32 : hi // 32].contiguous().view(E * HIDDEN, -1)
+        ).view(E, HIDDEN, -1)
+        self.k_wr = pack_bf16(self.w_r)
+        # the shared expert as vLLM stores it apart: row-major, scale per row
+        self.sh_rows = (
+            rows(q13)[N_EXPERTS],
+            rows(s13)[N_EXPERTS],
+            q2[N_EXPERTS, :, lo // 2 : hi // 2].contiguous(),
+            s2[N_EXPERTS, :, lo // 32 : hi // 32].contiguous(),
+        )
+        nmix = HC_MULT * (2 + HC_MULT)
+        self.fn = torch.randn(nmix, HC_MULT * HIDDEN, generator=g, device=device) * 0.01
+        self.scale = torch.rand(3, generator=g, device=device) + 0.5
+        self.base = torch.randn(nmix, generator=g, device=device) * 0.1
+        self.gamma = (
+            1 + 0.1 * torch.randn(HIDDEN, generator=g, device=device)
+        ).bfloat16()
+        self.g = g
+
+    def weights(self, separate: bool = False):
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.mono.config import N_EXPERTS
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.mono.ffn.op import (
+            FlashFfnWeights,
+        )
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.mono.packing import (
+            pack_shared_expert,
+        )
+
+        routed = (self.k_w13, self.k_s13, self.k_w2, self.k_s2)
+        if separate:
+            shared = pack_shared_expert(*self.sh_rows)
+            routed = tuple(t[:N_EXPERTS].contiguous() for t in routed)
+        else:
+            shared = tuple(t[N_EXPERTS] for t in routed)
+        return FlashFfnWeights(
+            w_r=self.k_wr,
+            bias=self.bias,
+            w_ug=routed[0],
+            s_ug=routed[1],
+            w_dn=routed[2],
+            s_dn=routed[3],
+            w_sh_ug=shared[0],
+            s_sh_ug=shared[1],
+            w_sh_dn=shared[2],
+            s_sh_dn=shared[3],
+            hc_fn=self.fn,
+            hc_scale=self.scale,
+            hc_base=self.base,
+            g_norm=self.gamma,

+def _check(rank: int, tp: int, device, separate: bool) -> None:

+    from vllm.distributed import get_tp_group

+        HC_MULT,
+        HIDDEN,

+    group = get_tp_group().cpu_group
+    # 16 TP2 rows overflow the down stage's LDS

+        op = FlashFfnOp(rt, lay.weights(separate), 0)
+        g = lay.g
+        parts = [

+            for _ in range(tp)

+        res = torch.randn(S, HC_MULT, HIDDEN, generator=g, device=device).bfloat16()
+        post = torch.rand(S, HC_MULT, 1, generator=g, device=device) * 2
+        comb = torch.softmax(
+            torch.randn(S, HC_MULT, HC_MULT, generator=g, device=device), -1
+        )

+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        assert not rt.words.any(), f"S={S}: expired waits {rt.words.tolist()}"
+

+            f"S={S}: ranks differ"

+        assert _rel(k_in, v_x) < 1e-2, f"S={S}: FFN input {_rel(k_in, v_x)}"
+

+        ref, order = _moe_reference(k_in, lay.w_r, lay.bias, lay.w13, lay.w2, 2048)

+                )

+        dist.barrier(group)
+        rt.close()
+

+    res = torch.randn(2, HC_MULT, HIDDEN, device=device).bfloat16()
+    post = torch.ones(2, HC_MULT, 1, device=device)

+"""GLM-5.3-Flash whole-layer KDA MonoKernel on CDNA4, one process a TP rank.
+
+Every stage is checked against vLLM's own ops on the kernel's own inputs to that
+stage: the attention-side mHC, the merged projection, the short conv, the gated
+delta rule (and both state updates), the gated RMSNorm, then the FFN seam on the
+TP sum of the o_proj partials and the MoE."""

+import torch

+from ._ffn import (
+    POLL_TIMEOUT_US,
+    REPLAYS,
+    _Layer,
+    _moe_reference,
+    _rel,
+    _vllm_seam,
+)
+
+ROWS = (2, 4, 8)
+SLOTS = 12
+
+
+class _Kda:
+    """One KDA layer's random attention weights (every rank builds the same) and
+    this rank's shard, in vLLM's post-load layouts."""
+
+    def __init__(self, rank: int, tp: int, device, tpr: int = 1) -> None:
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.mono.config import (
+            HC_MULT,
+            HIDDEN,
+            KDA_DIM,
+            KDA_HEADS,
+            KDA_PROJ,
+        )
+
+        g = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(1)
+        D, PF, HF = KDA_DIM, KDA_PROJ, KDA_HEADS
+        P, H = PF // tp, HF // tp
+        self.P, self.H, self.tp, self.rank = P, H, tp, rank
+
+        def rnd(*shape, scale=1.0):
+            return torch.randn(*shape, generator=g, device=device) * scale
+
+        nmix = HC_MULT * (2 + HC_MULT)
+        self.hc_fn = rnd(nmix, HC_MULT * HIDDEN, scale=0.01)
+        self.hc_scale = torch.rand(3, generator=g, device=device) + 0.5
+        self.hc_base = rnd(nmix, scale=0.1)
+        self.g_in = (1 + 0.1 * rnd(HIDDEN)).bfloat16()
+        wq, wk, wv = (rnd(PF, HIDDEN, scale=HIDDEN**-0.5) for _ in range(3))
+        wb = rnd(HF, HIDDEN, scale=HIDDEN**-0.5)
+        wfa, wga = (rnd(D, HIDDEN, scale=HIDDEN**-0.5) for _ in range(2))
+        self.w_fb_full = rnd(PF, D, scale=D**-0.5).bfloat16()
+        self.w_gb_full = rnd(PF, D, scale=D**-0.5).bfloat16()
+        self.w_o_full = rnd(HIDDEN, PF, scale=PF**-0.5).bfloat16()
+        conv = rnd(3, PF, 4, scale=0.5)
+        self.a_log_full = torch.log(torch.rand(HF, generator=g, device=device) * 8 + 1)
+        self.dt_full = rnd(PF, scale=0.5)
+        self.w_on = (1 + 0.1 * rnd(D)).float()
+
+        def sh(t, n):
+            return t[rank * n : (rank + 1) * n]
+
+        self.w_in = torch.cat(
+            [sh(wq, P), sh(wk, P), sh(wv, P), sh(wb, H), wfa, wga]
+        ).bfloat16()
+        self.w_fb = sh(self.w_fb_full, P).contiguous()
+        self.w_gb = sh(self.w_gb_full, P).contiguous()
+        self.w_o = self.w_o_full[:, rank * P : (rank + 1) * P].contiguous()
+        self.conv_w = torch.cat([sh(conv[i], P) for i in range(3)]).contiguous()
+        self.a_log = sh(self.a_log_full, H).contiguous()
+        self.dt_bias = sh(self.dt_full, P).contiguous()
+        # a verify step's conv state keeps one more column a draft token
+        self.conv0 = rnd(SLOTS, 3 * P, 2 + tpr).bfloat16()
+        self.rec0 = rnd(SLOTS, H, D, D, scale=0.05)
+
+    def weights(self):
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.mono.ffn.op import (
+            FlashKdaWeights,
+        )
+
+        return FlashKdaWeights(
+            hc_fn=self.hc_fn,
+            hc_scale=self.hc_scale,
+            hc_base=self.hc_base,
+            g_norm=self.g_in,
+            w_in=self.w_in,
+            w_fb=self.w_fb,
+            w_gb=self.w_gb,
+            conv_w=self.conv_w,
+            a_log=self.a_log,
+            dt_bias=self.dt_bias,
+            w_on=self.w_on,
+            w_o=self.w_o,
+        )

+def _seam(k: _Kda, x, res, post, comb):

+
+    lay = SimpleNamespace(fn=k.hc_fn, scale=k.hc_scale, base=k.hc_base, gamma=k.g_in)

+        num_accepted_tokens=acc,
+        query_start_loc=cu,
+        max_query_len=tpr,
+    )
+    qkv = causal_conv1d_update(
+        proj[:, : 3 * P].contiguous(),
+        conv if dim_first else conv.transpose(-1, -2),
+        k.conv_w,
+        None,
+        "silu",
+        **(spec if tpr > 1 else dict(conv_state_indices=idx)),
+    )
+    q, kk, v = (t.reshape(1, S, H, D) for t in qkv.split(P, dim=-1))
+    beta = proj[:, 3 * P : 3 * P + H].reshape(1, S, H).contiguous()
+    g1 = gates[:, :P].reshape(1, S, H, D).contiguous()
+    o, _ = fused_recurrent_kda(
+        q=q.contiguous(),
+        k=kk.contiguous(),
+        v=v.contiguous(),
+        g=g1,
+        beta=beta,
+        initial_state=rec,
+        use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True,
+        cu_seqlens=cu,
+        ssm_state_indices=idx.view(-1, tpr) if tpr > 1 else idx,
+        num_accepted_tokens=acc,
+        sigmoid_beta=True,
+        a_log=k.a_log.view(1, 1, H, 1),
+        g_bias=k.dt_bias,
+        compute_gate=True,
+        lower_bound=KDA_LOWER_BOUND,
+    )
+    with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()):
+        norm = FusedRMSNormGated(D, activation="sigmoid").to(proj.device)
+        norm.weight.data.copy_(k.w_on)
+        out = norm(o, gates[:, P:].reshape(S, H, D).contiguous())
+    return out.reshape(S, P)
+
+
+def _box(rt, name, n, packed=False):
+    """The first ``n`` values of a mailbox: f32 pairs, or packed bf16 pairs."""
+    words = rt.scratch[rt.sc[name] :].view(torch.int32)
+    if packed:
+        return words[:n:2].contiguous().view(torch.bfloat16)
+    return words[: 2 * n : 2].contiguous().view(torch.float32)
+
+
+def _check(rank: int, tp: int, device, dim_first: bool, tpr: int = 1) -> None:
+    import torch.distributed as dist
+
+    from vllm.distributed import get_tp_group
+    from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.mono.config import (
+        HC_MULT,
+        HIDDEN,
+        MOE_SLOTS,
+        FlashShard,
+    )
+    from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.specialized_decode.mono.ffn.op import (
+        FlashFfnOp,
+        FlashFfnRuntime,
+        FlashKdaState,
+    )
+
+    lay, kda = _Layer(rank, tp, device), _Kda(rank, tp, device, tpr)
+    if not dim_first:
+        kda.conv0 = kda.conv0.transpose(1, 2).contiguous()
+    n_in = FlashShard(tp).kda_in_rows
+    group = get_tp_group().cpu_group
+    rows = ROWS if tpr == 1 else [r * tpr for r in (1, 2, 4) if r * tpr <= 8]
+    for S in rows:
+        rt = FlashFfnRuntime(
+            S,
+            rank,
+            tp,
+            group,
+            2048 // tp,
+            1,
+            POLL_TIMEOUT_US,
+            False,
+            kda=True,
+            conv_dim_first=dim_first,
+            tpr=tpr,
+        )
+        op = FlashFfnOp(rt, lay.weights(), 0, kda.weights())
+        g = lay.g
+        x = torch.randn(S, HIDDEN, generator=g, device=device).bfloat16()
+        res = torch.randn(S, HC_MULT, HIDDEN, generator=g, device=device).bfloat16()
+        post = torch.rand(S, HC_MULT, 1, generator=g, device=device) * 2
+        comb = torch.softmax(
+            torch.randn(S, HC_MULT, HC_MULT, generator=g, device=device), -1
+        )
+        idx = torch.arange(1, S + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+        nreq = S // tpr
+        # the last request pads (when there is more than one)
+        pad = nreq > 1 or tpr == 1
+        if pad:
+            idx[S - tpr :] = -1
+        live = S - tpr if pad else S
+        acc = None
+        if tpr > 1:
+            acc = torch.randint(
+                1, tpr + 1, (nreq,), generator=g, device=device, dtype=torch.int32
+            )
+        kidx = idx if tpr == 1 else torch.cat([idx, acc])
+        state = FlashKdaState(kda.conv0.clone(), kda.rec0.clone())
+        dist.barrier(group)
+        outs = [t.clone() for t in op.launch(x, res, post, comb, state, kidx)]
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        assert not rt.words.any(), f"S={S}: expired waits {rt.words.tolist()}"
+        y, r2, p2, c2 = outs
+
+        gathered = [torch.empty_like(y).cpu() for _ in range(tp)]
+        dist.all_gather(gathered, y.cpu(), group=group)
+        assert all(torch.equal(gathered[0], o) for o in gathered), f"S={S}: ranks"
+
+        # attention-side mHC
+        ra, pa, ca, a_ref = _seam(kda, x, res, post, comb)
+        a_in = _box(rt, "a_in", S * HIDDEN, packed=True).view(S, HIDDEN)
+        assert _rel(a_in, a_ref) < 1e-2, f"S={S}: attention input {_rel(a_in, a_ref)}"
+
+        # merged projection and the f_b / g_b gates on the kernel's own inputs
+        proj = _box(rt, "proj", S * n_in).view(S, n_in)
+        want = (a_in.float() @ kda.w_in.float().T).bfloat16().float()
+        assert _rel(proj, want) < 1e-2, f"S={S}: projection {_rel(proj, want)}"
+        gates = _box(rt, "gates", S * 2 * kda.P).view(S, 2 * kda.P)
+        fa = proj[:, 3 * kda.P + kda.H :].bfloat16().float()
+        want = torch.cat(
+            [fa[:, :128] @ kda.w_fb.float().T, fa[:, 128:] @ kda.w_gb.float().T], 1
+        )
+        assert _rel(gates, want) < 1e-2, f"S={S}: gates {_rel(gates, want)}"
+
+        # short conv + gated delta rule + gated RMSNorm, and both state updates
+        conv, rec = kda.conv0.clone(), kda.rec0.clone()
+        o_ref = _kda_reference(
+            kda,
+            proj.bfloat16(),
+            gates.bfloat16(),
+            conv,
+            rec,
+            idx,
+            dim_first,
+            tpr,
+            acc,
+        )
+        o_in = _box(rt, "o_in", S * kda.P, packed=True).view(S, kda.P)
+        assert _rel(o_in[:live], o_ref[:live]) < 2e-2, (
+            f"S={S}: KDA output {_rel(o_in[:live], o_ref[:live])}"
+        )
+        assert _rel(state.conv_state, conv) < 1e-2, f"S={S}: conv state"
+        assert _rel(state.rec_state, rec) < 1e-3, (
+            f"S={S}: recurrent state {_rel(state.rec_state, rec)}"
+        )
+        top = int(idx.max()) + 1
+        assert torch.equal(state.rec_state[top:], kda.rec0[top:]), "untouched slots"
+
+        # FFN seam on the TP sum of every rank's o_proj partial
+        o_all = [torch.empty_like(o_in) for _ in range(tp)]
+        dist.all_gather(o_all, o_in.contiguous())
+        x_attn = torch.zeros(S, HIDDEN, device=device)
+        for r in range(tp):
+            w_o = kda.w_o_full[:, r * kda.P : (r + 1) * kda.P].float()
+            x_attn += (o_all[r].float() @ w_o.T).bfloat16().float()
+        v_r, v_p, v_c, v_x = _vllm_seam(lay, x_attn.bfloat16(), ra, pa, ca)
+        assert _rel(r2[:live], v_r[:live]) < 1e-3, f"S={S}: R'' {_rel(r2, v_r)}"
+        ep, ec = _rel(p2[:live], v_p[:live]), _rel(c2[:live], v_c[:live])
+        # as the sparse-attention test: the seam sums partials in a different order
+        assert ep < 1e-3 and ec < 1e-3, f"S={S}: post {ep}, comb {ec}"
+
+        a = rt.scratch[rt.sc["a"] :].view(torch.int32)[: S * HIDDEN : 2]
+        k_in = a.contiguous().view(torch.bfloat16).view(S, HIDDEN)
+        ref, order = _moe_reference(k_in, lay.w_r, lay.bias, lay.w13, lay.w2, 2048)
+        sel = rt.scratch[rt.sc["sel"] :].view(torch.int32)[: 2 * S * MOE_SLOTS : 2]
+        routed = sel.view(S, MOE_SLOTS)[:, 1:].sort(-1).values
+        assert torch.equal(routed[:live], order[:live].int().sort(-1).values)
+        assert _rel(y[:live], ref[:live]) < 5e-3, f"S={S}: MoE {_rel(y, ref)}"
+
+        if not pad:
+            dist.barrier(group)
+            rt.close()
+            continue
+        # a non-finite padding row stays in its own row
+        bad = x.clone()
+        bad[-1] = float("nan")
+        state_bad = FlashKdaState(kda.conv0.clone(), kda.rec0.clone())
+        dist.barrier(group)
+        rt.advance_step()
+        z = [t.clone() for t in op.launch(bad, res, post, comb, state_bad, kidx)]
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        for got, want in zip(z, outs):
+            assert torch.equal(got[:-1], want[:-1]), f"S={S}: a NaN row leaked"
+        assert torch.equal(state_bad.rec_state, state.rec_state)
+
+        # graph replays from the same state, every one bit for bit the first
+        dist.barrier(group)
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            state.conv_state.copy_(kda.conv0)
+            state.rec_state.copy_(kda.rec0)
+            rt.advance_step()
+            res_g = op.launch(x, res, post, comb, state, kidx)
+        for i in range(REPLAYS):
+            graph.replay()
+            if i % 100 == 99 or i == REPLAYS - 1:
+                torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+                assert all(torch.equal(o, w) for o, w in zip(res_g, outs)), (
+                    f"S={S}: replay {i} differs"
+                )
+        assert not rt.words.any()
+        dist.barrier(group)
+        rt.close()
